summary: Rebuilt the People (face enrolment) screen, and fixed the reason it never worked. THE FUNCTIONAL BUG: every request the page made was built as `${origin}/faces` with no `/api` prefix - the one screen in the app that had drifted from the `${apiBase()}/api/...` shape every other screen uses. The SPA's catch-all answers those paths with index.html and a 200, so the roster parsed an HTML page as its person list and rendered an empty, contented-looking screen, and 'Add person' reported success while creating nobody. The screen looked like it worked and did nothing at all. The page's fetch helper now throws on a 200 that is not JSON, so the same drift cannot come back silently. THE DESIGN: the page had NO stylesheet - it was written against a `.page`/`.page-head` vocabulary that has never existed in app.css, so every element fell back to browser defaults: bulleted lists, OS checkboxes and a bare file input. It now uses the app's own furniture (.workspace, .settings-panel, .toolbar) with a person-card roster, and the switch from the Dashboard's anomaly card moved into components/ui.js so both screens share one Toggle instead of two. THE MISSING HALF OF THE FEATURE: adding a person wrote a name and stopped. A person with no faceprints is skipped by the gallery export, so they are recognized by nothing - the screen now says that on the card, and adding somebody opens their enrolment dialog immediately. That dialog offers the two ways to supply a face side by side - files from this computer (picker or drag-and-drop) and a shot from this computer's own camera via getUserMedia - and lists the already-enrolled photos with per-photo delete, which finally calls the GET /api/faces/{id}/embeddings and DELETE /api/faces/embeddings/{id} routes the old screen never touched. Camera capture states the truth about secure contexts: browsers only hand over a camera on HTTPS or localhost, so on a plain http:// LAN address the pane says so instead of reporting a broken webcam. Server side: FaceEmbedding gained a Thumbnail column (the cropped face the model looked at, not the supplied photo) so enrolled shots can be seen and judged, and GET /api/faces now returns each person's faceprint count. Live-verified on a throwaway instance driven over CDP with Chrome's fake camera device: roster counts, camera rules created and deleted on the wire, a pause written through, a faceprint deleted, the capture path posting and the server's own rejection landing in the dialog - in English and Arabic (RTL), light and dark, with an empty console.
compatibility: Backward-compatible; no config change. NEW COLUMN: face_embedding.thumbnail, added additively by the auto-migrator on the next boot. Faceprints enrolled before it carry an empty string and show a placeholder tile in the enrolment dialog - nothing back-fills, because the original photos were never stored. GET /api/faces gains a `photos` field per person; existing fields are unchanged. No new routes: the enrolment dialog uses the embeddings routes that already shipped. Camera capture needs an HTTPS origin or localhost (a browser rule, not a product setting) and the page says so where it applies; uploading a photo works on any address. Enrolment still requires the face models on the host - the server's existing 'face models are not installed' message is now shown inline in the dialog. Frontend adds 43 dictionary keys in en/ms/zh/ar and drops the unused faces.enabled key; the built-in manual's People page is updated in all four languages.
